page: Amazon Web Services m7g.12xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 48 dedicated physical cores (48 vCPUs) running at 2.6 GHz with the AWS Neoverse-V1 model. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory capabilities. The server achieves top-tier memory performance, as evidenced by its PassMark memory score and high memory read/write bandwidths, reaching 4652.22 GB/sec cached and 252.61 GB/sec uncached. Multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, rank in the top 25%. It also demonstrates strong throughput in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, while single-core performance and text processing benchmarks fall within the average range.

The m7g.12xlarge offers a highly resource-dense profile, leveraging the ARM64 architecture to deliver high memory bandwidth and multi-core efficiency without the overhead of hyperthreading. However, the absence of local NVMe storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, though a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth helps mitigate this bottleneck. The instance is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, database hosting, Redis caching, and static web serving, while being less optimal for single-threaded tasks or heavy GPU-accelerated workloads.
